valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 27 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a Colombo-based licensed finance company (leases and stock out on hire about 38% and loans and advances about 44% of segment assets, the rest investments and other; Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 5), one sector. (2)–(3) A finance company, so no relevering: the sector's levered beta. Damodaran's emerging-markets file couldn't be opened from this run; the Financial Svcs. (Non-bank & Insurance) levered beta 0.97 (January 2026, web-search extract, as used for Commercial Credit and HNB Finance on this site) is used. (4) Local 5-year betas: none found from three sources in this run; the voting share trades thinly (2,738 public holders, 45% public; Interim p. 7), so local betas would be unreliable anyway. (5) 0.97. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7)–(8) Into scripts/reinvestment.py; shown as the Required return tile. Refresh in January 2027.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (27 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.97 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.2%, ±1.5 points. No WACC: a finance company's deposits and borrowings are its raw material, so it is valued on equity.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Company ROE 22.79% (2021/22), 9.08%, 13.1%, 18.15%, 17.21% (2025/26) (Annual Report 2025/26, pp. 10, 398); five-year average 16.1%. H1 2026/27 13.88% annualised (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 10); twelve months to Sep 15.6% (calculated). Base 16% assumes a partial recovery from this half as growth slows; bear 12% (between 2022/23 and 2023/24); bull 19% (2024/25 level plus some of the promised efficiency). Equity is 12.5% of assets and core capital 12.14%, so ROE can't be lifted much by more leverage.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Same in every method; below the 12.24% bond yield and the cost of equity, and below the 12.4% supported growth (Growth check).

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 4% / 7% / 9% (dividend growth for five years); supported 12.4% (72.1% of profit kept × 17.2% ROE). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: scripts/reinvestment.py on FY 2025/26: dividend Rs 1.75 of EPS Rs 6.28 (27.9% payout, note 15, p. 299) and ROE 17.21% (p. 10). Long-run growth 5–7% needs 42–37% of profit kept at 12–19% ROE, which the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE provides. Loan growth of 53% in 2025/26 was far above the supported rate and was funded by borrowing and a falling capital ratio, so it isn't assumed to repeat.

valuationInputs.name: Normal EPS 2026/27
valuationInputs.reason: H1 2026/27 EPS Rs 2.76 and Q2 Rs 1.38 (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 1): H1 × 2 and Q2 × 4 both Rs 5.52. Twelve-month run-rate Rs 5.96 (calculated: 6.28 + 2.76 − 3.08). Base Rs 5.60 is 6% below the run-rate (within the 10% rule): interest costs are rising faster than income (+56% vs +35% in H1) and gross NPL rose to 6.01%. Bear −19% for higher provisions; bull Rs 6.30 (the 2025/26 level).

valuationInputs.name: Dividends
valuationInputs.value: Next Rs 1.50 / 1.75 / 2.00, growing 4% / 7% / 9% for five years; then the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE (58% / 63% / 63%) of EPS
valuationInputs.reason: Rs 1.75 for 2025/26 (Rs 0.75 interim + Rs 1.00 final, note 15, p. 299), 27.9% of EPS; Rs 1.50 for 2024/25 (26.5%). Base keeps Rs 1.75 on similar EPS; bear cuts to Rs 1.50 as capital headroom narrows (core capital 12.14% vs 10% minimum); bull Rs 2.00.

valuationInputs.name: Residual income path
valuationInputs.value: ROE from 14% now to 12% / 16% / 19% over five years; payout 28%
valuationInputs.reason: Start: company ROE 13.88% for H1 2026/27 annualised (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 10). Payout = the 2025/26 dividend payout of 27.9% (p. 299).

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Justified P/B, P/E, dividend model, residual income
valuationInputs.reason: A finance company: book value and return on equity drive the value; no cash-flow DCF (CLAUDE.md: banks and finance companies).

openQuestions: Gross non-performing loans (6.01% at Sep 2026, up from 3.78%) and provision cover (37%) in the December quarter.
Net interest margin (6.37%) as funding costs rise and the CBSL's tighter vehicle loan-to-value caps bite.
Capital: core capital 12.14% against a 10% minimum; any rights issue or Tier 2 raise.
Whether the funding mix moves back towards deposits as promised (bank borrowing Rs 91.9bn vs deposits Rs 98.0bn).
Asia Management Capital Ventures' holdings (19.9% across four accounts) and the executive directors' margin-account buying.
Local 5-year betas from three sources (none found on 27 Nov 2026); refresh the beta in January 2027.

changeLog.basedOn: Annual Report 2025/26 and interims to 30 Jun and 30 Sep 2026
changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add CDB.N0000). First analysis: justified P/B, P/E, dividend model and residual income, all from scripts/valuation.py; beta 0.97 (finance sector, provisional), cost of equity 18.2%. Business tests 3 of 4 (fails steady profit), category 2 (watch list). Price is the 30 Sep 2026 last trade from the interim (Rs 32.50) because the CSE feed couldn't be reached from this run. Per-share figures are after the one-for-ten subdivision of April 2026 (company-restated). Ten-year summary used for 2016/17–2023/24; earlier year-end prices not read, so P/E history before 2024/25 is null. The annual report's investor-relations line giving Rs 262mn as the 2025/26 dividend total (p. 399) doesn't match note 15 or the Chairman's Rs 1.25bn and was not used.
